newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt up on speculation about Deuss.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt up on speculation about Deuss.

text.p: Shares in Karstadt AG surged on Thursday after a magazine report said major shareholders in the German retailer were in favour of a change in management.
Karstadt shares were up 10 marks at 547 marks, outpacing gains in the 30-share DAX index that was up 17.90 points at 3,262.92 points in pre-bourse IBIS electronic dealings.
Some traders said the gains in Karstadt, a member of the DAX index, were surprising and meant the market believed that Karstadt chief executive Walter Deuss would soon leave the retailer.
"It can only mean that investors are viewing the possible removal of Deuss from Karstadt as positive for the group," said one trader.
Germany's Wirtschaftswoche magazine said on Wednesday that large shareholders in Karstadt -- Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG -- were in favour of Deuss leaving the Cologne-based retailer.
The magazine also said Karstadt had lost almost 300 million marks ($178 million) in 1996, a reason one trader said could hardly explain the rise in Karstadt's shares on Thursday.
